---
title: "plainfeedback"
---

plainfeedback is open-source, self-hostable software for event-feedback surveys. You write a
survey as a plain markdown file; the app turns it into an accessible participant page, a
shareable link and QR code, and exports (CSV and JSONL) with a codebook per version. It is
designed to avoid collecting participant identifiers: no cookies, no IP or user-agent logging,
and a privacy statement on every survey.

It was built for the NIH Common Fund Data Ecosystem (CFDE) metrics effort, and suits any
consortium or group that runs recurring events and wants to move off one-off Google Forms and
Qualtrics.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Try it

A preview instance runs at **<https://plainfeedback.cancerdatasci.org>** (data may be wiped).
:::

## Who it is for

| You are | Start with |
|---|---|
| A survey author writing questions | [Writing a survey in markdown](grammar.md), then the [privacy statement template](privacy-statement-template.md) |
| Someone deploying it for a group | [Deploying plainfeedback](deploy.md) and [staff sign-in](deploy-auth.md); read the [threat model](threat-model.md) before collecting real responses |
| Automating surveys or exports | The [API guide](api.md), the [live API reference](https://plainfeedback.cancerdatasci.org/api/docs) and the [OpenAPI spec](openapi.json) |
| Reviewing how and why it was built | The [design](design.md), the [decision records](adr/0001-record-decisions.md) and the [phase-1 review](reviews/2026-10-14-phase-1.md) |

"Designed to avoid identifiers" is not a guarantee of anonymity: free text can identify
people, small groups can be re-identified, and proxies and CDNs can log IPs outside the app.
The [threat model](threat-model.md) says what is and is not protected.
